Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 27-Dec-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  OBJECT ORIENTED PROGRAMMING [IT_2122]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                       Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Explain how the StringBuffer class handles mutability and thread safety in Java. Compare it with  (5)  
  String and StringBuilder in terms of performance and synchronization. In what scenarios would you  
  A)           prefer StringBuffer over the other two?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Write a Java program named FindPrime that checks whether a given number is prime. Your                  (5)  
  program should:  
  
  Declare an integer variable num and assign it a value (e.g., 14).  
  Use a for loop to check if num is divisible by any number from 2 to num/2.  
  Use a boolean flag isPrime to track whether the number is prime.  
  Print "Prime" if the number is prime, otherwise print "Not Prime"  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Compare and contrast the types of inheritance supported in Java-single, multilevel, and                 (5)  
  hierarchical-by analyzing their structure and use cases. Examine why Java restricts multiple  
  A)           inheritance with classes, and evaluate how this design choice affects ambiguity and method  
  resolution.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Write a Java program that demonstrates hierarchical inheritance:                                        (5)  
  
  Class Vehicle with a method startEngine()  
  Class Car and class Bike both extend Vehicle  
  Override startEngine() in both Car and Bike to provide specific messages  
  In the main method, create objects of Car and Bike and call startEngine() on each.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                Analyze the structure and behavior of a Java program that defines and uses a custom exception    (5)  
  class named InvalidAgeException. Break down how throw, throws, and exception class inheritance  
  A)           are used to enforce age validation. Examine the interaction between try-catch-finally blocks and  
  explain how control flow is affected when the age is less than 18. Use code examples to support  
  your analysis.  
  
  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)               Describe the different states a thread can be in (New, Runnable, Running, Blocked, Terminated).     (5)  
  How does the Thread class manage thread priorities, and what is the impact of using set Priority()?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)                       Explain how generics improve type safety and code reusability. Write a simple generic class Box<     (5)  
  T> that stores a value of type T and includes methods to set and get the value.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)               Analyze the roles and relationships among the JavaFX components: Application class, Stage,           (5)  
  Scene, and Node. How do these components interact to form a GUI structure? Compare this  
  architecture with AWT and Swing, highlighting key differences in design and functionality  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)                       CERT recommends preserving the cause of an exception when rethrowing it. Explain why it's            (5)  
  important to use exception chaining (throw new Exception(e)) instead of discarding the original  
  A)               exception.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)               Apply the principles of encapsulation by implementing a Java class Student with the following        (5)  
  access constraints: name as read-only, rollNumber as write-only, and grade as read-write. Use  
  appropriate access modifiers and provide only the necessary getter/setter methods. In the main  
  method, demonstrate how to interact with each field according to its access level.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  -----End-----
